title: Can LP2 words be shifted dictionary words?
question: Do complete LP2 words of four to eight runes match a pinned dictionary under Caesar or affine word-level maps more often than uniform-random rune words?
reader_question: Could each LP2 word simply be a shifted dictionary word?
summary: A pinned source replay finds no Caesar-pattern matches among 628 LP2 words of six to eight runes; short-word and affine matches are common under the source's random-word comparison.
finding: For lengths four through eight, Caesar-pattern matches are 165/511, 12/317, 0/256, 0/216 and 0/156. The original 2,000-word-per-length random control gives 627, 45, 4, 0 and 0. Affine match rates resemble that control. The published 'reversed' operator reverses a difference tuple, which is not literal word reversal.
limitations: Results depend on the pinned external dictionary, relikd word segmentation and source random baseline. A lack of dictionary-pattern hits does not rule out other vocabularies, hidden word boundaries, longer transforms or plaintext recovery. The source dictionary and page files have not been redistributed.
next_steps: A more specific wordwise proposal should freeze a vocabulary, boundary rule and transform before testing held-out pages, then compare its matches with controls that preserve the same word-length distribution.

scope.representation: Nine pinned unsolved relikd sections, 12,956 rune symbols, full source-visible words of rune lengths 4–8. The 18 source page files and source rune dictionary are SHA-256 pinned but must be obtained separately.
scope.procedure: Build sets of mod-29 neighboring-rune difference tuples from the dictionary, then count exact Caesar, source-reversed-difference, literal reversed-word Caesar and affine-normalized membership. Compare source's 2,000 uniform-random words per length and solved LP1 plaintext.
scope.parameters: GP29; word lengths 4–8; random.Random(1) continuously across lengths; 2,000 random words per length.
scope.exclusions: Other dictionaries, alternative segmentation, per-word key inference beyond tuple membership, whole-page readability and all other cipher families.

review.reviewer: Independent arithmetic and pinned-source receipt checker

reproduction.environment: Python 3.9+ standard library; source-root must be relikd/LiberPrayground at pinned revision and is hash-checked. Upstream code and corpus are not copied into this record.
